Join our movement, be part of the progress, and help ensure a healthier future for all. You matter, and so does the impact you can make with us.

We are currently hiring a Senior Development Director based in Sacramento. This leader will cultivate and engage volunteers, companies and community stakeholders in advancing the mission of the American Heart Association and drive meaningful support and revenue growth for the Heart and Stroke Walk event in Sacramento.

This position is based in the Sacramento, Stockton & Modesto division and the work is wherever it is most effective – in the field, at home and in our Sacramento office.

We have a fast-paced sales type of environment with the main responsibility of driving revenue in support of our mission. We offer a base salary with the potential to earn an incentive up to 25% of your base pay. The potential incentive is based on achieving certain revenue targets and triggers.

With an aging society, obesity and diabetes on the rise, and an uptick in surgical procedures, the number of patients with non-healing wounds that would benefit from expert care is dramatically increasing. As a result, the company is working to provide our differentiated, quality outcomes to as many patients that would benefit through our out-patient clinic partnerships

The Program Director or Program Manager is responsible for the management and the strategic growth of the Wound Care Program for the assigned area of responsibility. This position is responsible for the complete oversight of the Wound Care Center, to include the following functions: day-to-day center operations, staff management, financial management, quality/performance improvement, and community education. The Program Director/Program Manager is also responsible for maintaining collaborative and consultative client relationships within and outside the hospital organization and for creating effective working relationships between Healogics and the hospital.

All Healogics employees must perform their job responsibilities according to all Healogics policies, Hospital policies, as well as to accrediting organizations, federal and state regulation, and to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) guidelines, as applicable.

Essential Functions/Responsibilities: (Percentage times shown in parenthesis next to each function)

Manages the Center’s Operations (20%):

Oversees the day-to-day management of outpatient clinic(s) and other wound continuum programs, as applicable.
Continuously assesses current clinic flows, processes and procedures, identifies areas of improvement, and develops and implements best practices and appropriate changes to improve outcomes, using the company’s resources.
Works with hospital and company personnel to ensure availability of adequate resources, supplies, equipment and services.
Facilitates the flow of information and maximizes effective communication throughout the program.
Prioritizes responsibilities and directs the work of the Center’s clinical staff and non- clinical staff.

Manages direct reports in conjunction with the company and hospital HR departments. This includes interviewing, hiring, motivating, coaching, counselling, establishing performance expectations, and conducting performance reviews. (5%)

jobs.description:
About CCA

Founded in 1989, the Center for Community Advocacy (CCA) develops leadership among farmworkers and low-income families across the Salinas and Pajaro Valleys. Through neighborhood-based committees (comités), CCA supports community members in advocating for improved housing, health, economic conditions, and opportunities. Nearly four decades in, CCA is a trusted institution with deep community relationships, a committed team, and a strong history of grassroots leadership development.
The Opportunity

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director serves as CCA's chief executive and provides strategic, organizational, and operational leadership across programs and services, fundraising and external relations, finance and administration, people and organizational leadership, advocacy, and Board partnership. The Executive Director oversees approximately 10 staff and an annual operating budget of approximately $2 million.
This is an opportunity for a leader who is equally comfortable building authentic community relationships, developing staff and organizational capacity, partnering strategically with a Board, cultivating funders and partners, and advancing the voices and priorities of farmworkers and low-income families.
A KEY EARLY PRIORITY

Strengthen CCA's fundraising infrastructure and help establish a sustainable development function during the first year.
THE LEADERSHIP OPPORTUNITY

Build on a trusted organization's foundation while strengthening strategy, people, systems, partnerships, and long-term sustainability.

We Are Looking for a Leader Who

·        Is deeply committed to social justice, community empowerment, and CCA's mission.
·        Builds trust and authentic relationships with community members, staff, funders, partners, and Board members.
·        Brings strong organizational leadership experience, including staff supervision and financial oversight.
·        Has demonstrated experience in diversified fundraising and relationship-building with funders, donors, partners, and stakeholders.
·        Can provide strategic leadership while remaining connected to the day-to-day realities of a community-based organization.
·        Develops people, strengthens organizational culture, and builds accountable and effective teams.
·        Can serve as a strong external voice and advocate for farmworkers, low-income families, and the communities CCA serves.
·        Is bilingual in English and Spanish with the proficiency needed to communicate effectively with CCA's community, staff, Board, funders, and other stakeholders.
Preferred experience includes:
building or scaling a development function; farmworker, tenant, or immigrant-rights organizing; nonprofit financial management and grants; partnering with nonprofit Boards; leading through organizational change; union environments; and community-led leadership models.
Compensation & Benefits

The salary range is $105,000-$125,000, commensurate with experience. CCA offers medical, dental, and vision benefits; a pension program; vacation; holidays; and sick leave. The position is based across CCA's Salinas and Castroville offices, with regular travel into the community and some evening and weekend availability.
How to Apply

Please email the following application materials to careers@cca-viva.org
:
·        Cover letter
·        Resume
·        List of four professional references
Priority Screening Date: September 30, 2026
 | Position will remain open until filled.
Join CCA in developing community leadership, strengthening collective voice, and expanding opportunities for farmworkers and low-income families across California's Central Coast.

About The Agency

The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City. As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.

Your Team

The Office of Investigations and Labor Relations (OILR), part of the Office of the First Deputy Commissioner at the Department of Housing Preservation and Development, supports the agency’s mission by serving all divisions and offices to address a wide range of operational and personnel matters across the organization.

Your Impact

HPD is an agency of over 2,000 employees dispersed among multiple divisions responsible for everything from enforcing housing code, developing new building projects, and administering the Section 8 program. The candidate will be expected to perform highly confidential and sensitive investigations into misconduct and incompetence of all agency employees, looking into issues ranging from performance to falsifying records to criminal behavior, as well as assist in navigating relations between management and labor unions regarding employee concerns.

Your Role

The role of the Deputy Director of OILR will be conducting investigations, supervising subordinate staff investigating allegations of employee misconduct, assigning work to investigators, and training new employees.

As a Deputy Director, the candidate will fill in for the Director managing investigations and dealing with labor issues when they are absent from the office. They will provide recommendations on punitive and restorative actions and advise on resolutions to organizational challenges. Additionally, the candidate will be running the Critical Driver program for the entire Agency, coordinating with General Services and driver liaisons across every Division. They will assume responsibility for OILR's internal special projects, such as digitizing old disciplinary cases and creating a training manual for future investigators.

Your Responsibilities

The primary duties and responsibilities of the Deputy Director of OILR will be to

Conduct and supervise investigations into employee misconduct.
Train and supervise interns and college aides who work in the unit on various projects.
Serve as a key problem-solver and subject matter expert on disciplinary issues and dispute resolution and provide recommendations to senior staff on organizational or policy changes.
Serves as a liaison with municipal labor unions on various labor-management issues, resolve employee grievances, and facilitate labor-management meetings.
Plan and coordinate investigation schedules and assignments.
Prepare, review, evaluate, and act on all reports and recommendations submitted for administrative action.
Supervise training programs.
Administer the Critical Driver program and other projects.
Occasionally serve notices on employees and assist in surveillance.

MISSION & ABOUT AUERFARM:

Inspiring children and adults to engage in, learn about, and enjoy agriculture, science, and the natural environment.

The 4-H Education Center at Auerfarm is a vibrant 120-acre nonprofit farm and educational center located in Bloomfield, CT. For generations, Auerfarm has connected people of all ages to agriculture, science, environmental stewardship, and the natural world through hands-on learning and community engagement.

The Cooper Foundation is currently seeking an Executive Director (ED) to provide visionary leadership, strategic direction and operational oversight. The ED will work closely with the Board of Directors to fulfill the organization's mission and maximize community impact in the Raleigh / NC service area and oversee the Foundation’s expansion to Atlanta. The ED is responsible for working with the organization’s partners to fulfill housing stability grant requests, identifying strategic partners, fundraising, coordinating with Cooper Tacia’s finance and marketing teams, and engaging with the community.

Background

Founded in 2023, the Cooper Charitable Foundation was created with the mission to improve people’s lives by helping them secure stable housing. John Cooper, our founder, and his family come from quite humble beginnings. Each of them understands the power of stability and safety in changing the trajectory of one's life. The Cooper Foundation was created to honor his own family and to express gratitude for his journey. 

John learned about transitional housing grants while involved with Haven in Lee County, a non-profit providing assistance to victims of domestic violence and sexual assault. The Cooper Charitable Foundation adapted this concept and created Housing Stability Grants to address the critical issue of housing accessibility in our communities.

Our grants provide financial assistance in two ways – helping working people access housing or preventing people from being evicted due to life circumstances.

The majority of our grants help people pay move-in fees such as security deposits, utility deposits and first and last month’s rent. What we discovered is that many unsheltered people are working; they can pay their rent, but they can’t save enough money for the upfront fees required by most landlords. This is the biggest barrier to safe and accessible housing.

We also assist those who are working but cannot keep up with their monthly expenses due to life circumstances. Issues such as illness, mental health, a car accident, job loss, divorce or domestic violence can all impact people’s lives in different ways. We help people pay their rent and utilities or pay for car repairs or other expenses.

Shared Development Director: Independent Contractor

RefugeeConnect & Immigrant and Refuge Law Center

Greater Cincinnati • Hybrid/Remote

Contract Amount: $55,000

A Unique Shared Development Opportunity

RefugeeConnect and the Immigrant and Refugee Law Center (IRLC) are seeking an experienced development professional to serve as our Shared Development Director
, an independent contractor providing strategic fundraising and development support across both organizations.

This is not a traditional Development Director role. It is a unique opportunity to work alongside two established Greater Cincinnati nonproﬁts serving refugee and immigrant communities while helping us explore what becomes possible when mission-aligned organizations intentionally share expertise, resources, relationships, and fundraising strategy.

The Shared Development Director will support the distinct development priorities of RefugeeConnect and IRLC while also identifying opportunities for collaboration, including shared funding opportunities, donor and corporate engagement, joint fundraising initiatives, and long-range planning connected to a future regional welcoming center.

The ideal contractor will be comfortable navigating multiple organizational priorities, building relationships, developing systems, and moving between strategy and implementation. We are looking for someone who sees collaboration not as an added responsibility, but as an opportunity to build stronger and more sustainable organizations.

About the Partnership

RefugeeConnect and IRLC are two independent organizations with complementary roles in supporting refugees and immigrants throughout Greater Cincinnati.

RefugeeConnect
walks alongside refugees and their families, connecting them to resources, relationships, guidance, and opportunities to enhance their lives and thrive in our shared community.

The Immigrant and Refugee Law Center (IRLC)
provides accessible legal services to immigrant and refugee families in the Greater Cincinnati community.

Through an ongoing organizational partnership, RefugeeConnect and IRLC are investing in shared capacity that strengthens each organization individually while creating opportunities to collaborate around funding, community partnerships, and a longer-term vision for stronger regional welcoming infrastructure.

About the Contract

The Shared Development Director will provide development expertise across three interconnected areas:
Supporting the individual fundraising and development priorities of RefugeeConnect; Supporting the
individual fundraising and development priorities of IRLC; and
Identifying and advancing collaborative opportunities that beneﬁt both organizations and their shared long-term goals.

The contractor will work collaboratively with organizational leadership while maintaining the ability to independently organize and carry out the services and deliverables outlined in the contract.

Scope of Services

Funding Strategy & Opportunity Development

Research and identify foundation, private, corporate, sponsorship, and other funding opportunities aligned with the missions and strategic priorities of both organizations.

Develop and maintain funding pipelines and prospect tracking systems, identify opportunities appropriate for collaborative applications, and provide leadership with regular funding research, recommendations, and timelines.

Donor Engagement, Stewardship & Prospect Development

Strengthen donor management and stewardship practices for both organizations, including donor tracking, segmentation, engagement planning, retention analysis, and cultivation strategies.

Conduct prospect research to identify potential individual donors, philanthropic partners, corporate supporters, sponsors, and other strategic relationships.

Fundraising Campaigns, Events & Sponsorships

Support the planning and implementation of annual fundraising campaigns and donor engagement initiatives for both organizations.

Assist with fundraising events, sponsorship development, donor engagement strategies, and collaborative fundraising activities, including at least one joint fundraising initiative during the contract period.

Long-Range Funding Strategy

Support both organizations in developing diversiﬁed, sustainable long-term funding strategies.

Research institutional funding, corporate partnerships, major donor opportunities, sponsorships, earned revenue strategies, and potential future capital support.
Provide strategic research and recommendations to strengthen organizational readiness for future growth and fundraising opportunities.

Regional Welcoming Center Planning

Support RefugeeConnect and IRLC's exploration of a future regional welcoming center by researching successful models and sustainable funding strategies and helping identify potential philanthropic, corporate, technical, and community partners.

The contractor will contribute to collaborative visioning, relationship development, strategic planning, and early capital campaign and feasibility research associated with this longer-term initiative.

Why This Role Is Different

Shared positions require a different kind of development professional.

The Shared Development Director will have the opportunity to strengthen fundraising capacity within two independent organizations while helping us build a thoughtful model for collaboration between them.

Success in this role requires someone who can understand the unique mission, priorities, culture, donors, and funding needs of each organization while recognizing opportunities where working together can create greater impact.

For someone who enjoys building systems, cultivating relationships, identifying opportunities, and helping organizations think strategically about what's next, this contract offers the opportunity to help shape something genuinely different.

Work Arrangement

This is a hybrid-remote contract opportunity based in Greater Cincinnati
.

The contractor will have signiﬁcant ﬂexibility to complete research, writing, planning, prospect development, and administrative work remotely. The role also requires availability to participate in in-person donor meetings, organizational meetings, fundraising events, collaborative planning sessions, community meetings, and other relationship-building activities throughout Greater Cincinnati as appropriate to the work.

Because relationship-building is an important component of the engagement, applicants should be based in or able to regularly work in the Greater Cincinnati region.

Ideal Experience

We are interested in hearing from experienced development professionals and consultants who bring a combination of strategic thinking, relationship-building skills, and hands-on fundraising experience.
Competitive candidates may demonstrate experience in areas such as:

Nonproﬁt fundraising and fund development;
Foundation, corporate, and institutional fundraising;
Grant prospect research and funding pipeline development;
Individual donor cultivation and stewardship;
Major donor and prospect research;
Fundraising campaigns and events;
Corporate sponsorships and partnerships;
Donor database or CRM strategy;
Development planning and revenue diversiﬁcation;
Capital campaign or feasibility research;
Working across multiple organizations, partnerships, coalitions, or collaborative initiatives; and
Building development systems and strategies within growing organizations.

We especially welcome candidates who are comfortable working independently, managing multiple priorities, building relationships across organizations, and helping translate ambitious ideas into practical fundraising strategies.

About BeFit Rehabilitation
BeFit Rehabilitation provides Medicare Part B outpatient physical, occupational, and speech therapy within assisted living facilities across the Tampa/Clearwater area. As we scale, we're building the operational infrastructure to match our clinical growth — this role is central to that effort.

Position Summary
The Regional Director of Operations owns the operational and financial performance of BeFit's therapy teams across all locations. This is not a clinical-oversight-only role — it is a hands-on operational leadership position responsible for staffing efficiency, revenue cycle performance, and regulatory compliance, with direct accountability for the P&L of each care team. The ideal candidate has run multi-site outpatient therapy operations before, understands Medicare Part B billing and PTA/COTA supervision rules deeply, and has a track record of turning around underperforming locations or teams.

This role reports directly to the President and will work closely with billing, HR, and clinical leadership.

Key Responsibilities
Staffing & Productivity Management

Own visit-per-hour and revenue-per-hour benchmarks for every clinical team; identify and correct gaps between hours paid and billable production
Right-size supervising-therapist-to-assistant ratios based on actual patient census and caseload, not headcount assumptions
Partner with clinical leadership to set and enforce productivity standards across PT, OT, and ST disciplines
Build and maintain a recurring reporting cadence (weekly/monthly) that surfaces cost-per-hour vs. collections-per-hour by team and by office

Revenue Cycle & AR Oversight

Own aging AR across all payers; drive resolution of denied and zero-paid claims, with particular focus on Medicare Part B and any payer showing systemic non-payment
Work directly with billing/clearinghouse partners on root-cause analysis of denial patterns (not just resubmission)
Establish escalation protocols for payers showing abnormal payment failure rates
Monitor and report true collection rates against payer-adjudicated allowables (not charge amounts)

Compliance & Documentation

Ensure correct and consistent use of billing modifiers across all supervising clinicians
Audit documentation-to-billing alignment periodically to catch under- or over-utilization of assistant modifiers before it becomes an audit risk
Maintain compliance with CMS supervision, evaluation-complexity coding, and Part B billing requirements across all offices

Financial Accountability

Build and maintain a per-team/per-office P&L model (labor cost vs. collections) and present it to leadership on a regular cycle
Flag underperforming teams early, with a specific, data-backed diagnosis (productivity vs. collections vs. staffing mix) rather than a general "revenue is down" alert
Partner with leadership on compensation structure design (salary vs. per-visit vs. per-unit) to ensure pay models align incentives with actual reimbursement economics

Team Leadership & Multi-Site Operations

Serve as the operational point of contact across all facility partnerships
Support hiring, onboarding, and performance management for clinical and support staff in partnership with HR
Identify and roll out best practices from top-performing teams to underperforming ones

Qualifications
Required

5+ years in outpatient therapy operations management, ideally spanning multiple sites or facilities
Deep working knowledge of Medicare Part B billing, PTA/COTA supervision and reimbursement rules (including CQ/CO modifier requirements), and CPT coding for PT/OT/ST
Demonstrated experience building or managing productivity and financial performance metrics for clinical teams (not just clinical quality metrics)
Track record of identifying and resolving AR/denial issues at scale
Comfortable working directly from raw billing, payroll, and revenue data not just dashboards

Preferred

Experience specifically in ALF, SNF, or senior-living-adjacent outpatient therapy settings
Prior experience turning around an underperforming location, region, or book of business
Familiarity with per-visit and per-unit compensation models for PT/OT/ST staff and their financial implications
Clinical licensure (PT, OT, or SLP) is a plus but not required if operational/financial background is strong

Full visibility into every team's cost-per-hour vs. collections-per-hour; a clear, documented diagnosis of the 2-3 highest-impact underperforming teams or offices.
6 months:
Measurable improvement in the lowest-performing teams' hours-to-collections ratio; AR aging materially reduced on the largest payer categories; a standing compliance review process for assistant modifier usage in place.
Ongoing:
A durable, repeatable operating rhythm — not a one-time fix — where staffing decisions, compensation structure, and payer issues are caught and addressed before they become a multi-month drag on the P&L.

About the Role

Kids’ Meals is seeking an accomplished, mission-driven Senior Director of Advancement to provide strategic fundraising for the organization, from annual, mid-level, major, recurring, and planned giving donors.

This position develops and executes strategies to acquire, cultivate, solicit, steward, and increase giving from individual and foundation donors while building a sustainable pipeline that supports Kids’ Meals’ long-term revenue goals. The Senior Director will manage a portfolio of prospects capable of making gifts of $5,000 or more.

Reporting to the Chief Advancement Officer, the Senior Director partners closely with the CEO, Board of Directors, and Development and Communications team to expand philanthropic revenue, strengthen donor relationships, and create meaningful donor experiences connected to the mission of ending childhood hunger.

Key Responsibilities

Donor Strategy:
Develop and execute a comprehensive strategy to grow annual, mid-level, major, recurring, and planned giving revenue.
Revenue Performance:
Establish and achieve revenue, donor acquisition, retention, , and pipeline development goals in partnership with the Chief Advancement Officer.
Portfolio Management:
Build and manage a portfolio of approximately 100 prospects capable of making gifts of $5,000 or more.
Major Gift Fundraising:
Personally cultivate, solicit, and steward donors and prospects, with an emphasis on securing five- and six-figure gifts.
Moves Management:
Design and implement processes and tracking systems that support consistent donor identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
Executive Partnership:
Partner with the Chief Advancement Officer and CEO on the cultivation and solicitation of board members, community leaders, high-capacity prospects, and other priority donors.

Oversee annual giving campaigns, giving circles, recurring donor programs, and other opportunities to increase donor engagement and long-term support.
Planned Giving:
Develop and grow the organization’s planned giving program through prospect identification, donor education, cultivation, recognition, and stewardship.
Donor Stewardship:
Develop and oversee stewardship efforts that recognizes, engages, and retains donors at all giving levels.
Donor Communications:
Collaborate with the Communications team to create donor-centered appeals, impact stories, campaign materials, and stewardship communications.
Donor Engagement:
Partner with the Special Events and Volunteer Experience teams to create meaningful mission-focused experiences for donors.
Data and Reporting:
Use donor and giving data to identify trends, segment audiences, evaluate performance, and uncover opportunities for donor acquisition and increased giving.

Partner with Finance and Development Operations to support accurate gift processing, reconciliation, revenue tracking, budgeting, and forecasting.

Experience building donor pipelines and using moves management to advance prospects through cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.

Control testing for design and operating effectiveness is performed by the Controls Assurance Testing (CAT) team; this role does not execute independent testing directly but sets requirements, engages closely with CAT throughout the testing cycle, and is accountable for the overall compliance outcome. The Executive Director builds and leads a team focused on scoping, evidence governance, audit coordination, and executive reporting, and drives close partnership with CAT to ensure testing is scoped, resourced, and completed on schedule.

Key Responsibilities

Own the enterprise SOX cybersecurity/ITGC and SOC 1/SOC 2 compliance programs end-to-end from a first-line perspective, including control scope definition, requirements, evidence standards, and readiness activities, in coordination with Finance, control owners, Internal Audit, and external auditors.
Partner closely with the Controls Assurance Testing (CAT) team to define the annual testing scope and calendar, ensure testing requirements and evidence standards are clearly understood, and resolve scoping or interpretation questions; engage with CAT throughout the testing cycle to monitor progress, address blockers, and ensure control owners provide evidence and support on schedule.
Lead SOC 1 and SOC 2 readiness activities, including control mapping to trust services criteria and coordination with CAT and control owners on evidence collection ahead of attestation testing.

Own the control deficiency lifecycle from a first-line compliance-program perspective — reviewing CAT's testing results, driving root cause analysis and remediation planning with control owners, and coordinating closure readiness with Internal Audit and external auditors — with clear accountability assigned to control and process owners.
Maintain SOX and SOC control requirements, scoping documentation, and evidence standards within GRC platforms (e.g., AuditBoard, Archer), ensuring CAT and control owners are working from current, assurance-ready requirements.
Drive continuous improvement of SOX and SOC compliance processes, including evidence-reuse and reduction of duplicative requests to control owners, in partnership with CAT and GRC tooling teams.
Produce and present executive-level reporting on SOX and SOC compliance posture, control readiness, tested control effectiveness (sourced from CAT's testing results), issue trends, and remediation progress to AVP GRC, Deputy CISO, and relevant governance forums.
Partner with policy and standards owners to ensure SOX and SOC control requirements reflect current regulatory and framework expectations as they evolve.
Support the security exception and risk acceptance process for SOX- and SOC-relevant control gaps identified through CAT's testing, ensuring appropriate documentation and executive visibility.
Lead, coach, and develop the SOX & SOC Compliance team, building bench strength and a culture of accountability, precision, and strong cross-team partnership with CAT.

10+ years of progressive experience leading first-line-of-defense SOX ITGC, SOC 1/SOC 2, technology compliance, or control governance programs, including 3+ years in a leadership role.

Think you are a great fit? Learn more about this role here:

Healogics is the largest provider of advanced wound care services in the United States, treating more than 300,000 chronic wound patients annually across over 600 sites. With an aging society, obesity and diabetes on the rise, and an uptick in surgical procedures, the number of patients with non-healing wounds that would benefit from expert care is dramatically increasing. As a result, the company is working to provide our differentiated, quality outcomes to as many patients that would benefit through our out-patient clinic partnerships

The Program Director or Program Manager is responsible for the management and the strategic growth of the Wound Care Program for the assigned area of responsibility. This position is responsible for the complete oversight of the Wound Care Center, to include the following functions: day-to-day center operations, staff management, financial management, quality/performance improvement, and community education. The Program Director/Program Manager is also responsible for maintaining collaborative and consultative client relationships within and outside the hospital organization and for creating effective working relationships between Healogics and the hospital.

All Healogics employees must perform their job responsibilities according to all Healogics policies, Hospital policies, as well as to accrediting organizations, federal and state regulation, and to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) guidelines, as applicable.

Manages the Center’s Operations (20%):

Works with hospital and company personnel to ensure availability of adequate resources, supplies, equipment and services.
Facilitates the flow of information and maximizes effective communication throughout the program.
Prioritizes responsibilities and directs the work of the Center’s clinical staff and non- clinical staff.

Manages direct reports in conjunction with the company and hospital HR departments. This includes interviewing, hiring, motivating, coaching, counselling, establishing performance expectations, and conducting performance reviews. (5%)

Performs Financial Management (10%)

Manages and coordinates all aspects of the revenue cycle for Healogics and for the hospital partner, as appropriate.

Manages costs through appropriate utilization and management of labor and supply.

About CCA

Founded in 1989, the Center for Community Advocacy (CCA) develops leadership among farmworkers and low-income families across the Salinas and Pajaro Valleys. Through neighborhood-based committees (comités), CCA supports community members in advocating for improved housing, health, economic conditions, and opportunities. Nearly four decades in, CCA is a trusted institution with deep community relationships, a committed team, and a strong history of grassroots leadership development.
The Opportunity

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director serves as CCA's chief executive and provides strategic, organizational, and operational leadership across programs and services, fundraising and external relations, finance and administration, people and organizational leadership, advocacy, and Board partnership. The Executive Director oversees approximately 10 staff and an annual operating budget of approximately $2 million.
This is an opportunity for a leader who is equally comfortable building authentic community relationships, developing staff and organizational capacity, partnering strategically with a Board, cultivating funders and partners, and advancing the voices and priorities of farmworkers and low-income families.
A KEY EARLY PRIORITY

Strengthen CCA's fundraising infrastructure and help establish a sustainable development function during the first year.
THE LEADERSHIP OPPORTUNITY

Build on a trusted organization's foundation while strengthening strategy, people, systems, partnerships, and long-term sustainability.

We Are Looking for a Leader Who

·        Is deeply committed to social justice, community empowerment, and CCA's mission.
·        Builds trust and authentic relationships with community members, staff, funders, partners, and Board members.
·        Brings strong organizational leadership experience, including staff supervision and financial oversight.
·        Has demonstrated experience in diversified fundraising and relationship-building with funders, donors, partners, and stakeholders.
·        Can provide strategic leadership while remaining connected to the day-to-day realities of a community-based organization.
·        Develops people, strengthens organizational culture, and builds accountable and effective teams.
·        Can serve as a strong external voice and advocate for farmworkers, low-income families, and the communities CCA serves.
·        Is bilingual in English and Spanish with the proficiency needed to communicate effectively with CCA's community, staff, Board, funders, and other stakeholders.
Preferred experience includes:
building or scaling a development function; farmworker, tenant, or immigrant-rights organizing; nonprofit financial management and grants; partnering with nonprofit Boards; leading through organizational change; union environments; and community-led leadership models.
Compensation & Benefits

The salary range is $105,000-$125,000, commensurate with experience. CCA offers medical, dental, and vision benefits; a pension program; vacation; holidays; and sick leave. The position is based across CCA's Salinas and Castroville offices, with regular travel into the community and some evening and weekend availability.
How to Apply

Please email the following application materials to careers@cca-viva.org
:
·        Cover letter
·        Resume
·        List of four professional references

About The Agency

The Department of Housing Preservation and Development (HPD) oversees housing standards across all 3.7 million homes in New York City. As the nation’s largest municipal housing agency, HPD is responsible for building and preserving affordable housing, protecting tenants from harassment and displacement, and holding landlords accountable across the five boroughs. Under Commissioner Dina Levy and the Mamdani Administration, HPD is pursuing an ambitious housing agenda focused on the needs of New York’s tenants. With a broad set of tools including standards enforcement, tenant resources, and the creation of new affordable housing, HPD is committed to making New York City a more affordable place for renters and homeowners alike.

Your Team

The Office of Investigations and Labor Relations (OILR), part of the Office of the First Deputy Commissioner at the Department of Housing Preservation and Development, supports the agency’s mission by serving all divisions and offices to address a wide range of operational and personnel matters across the organization.

Your Impact

HPD is an agency of over 2,000 employees dispersed among multiple divisions responsible for everything from enforcing housing code, developing new building projects, and administering the Section 8 program. The candidate will be expected to perform highly confidential and sensitive investigations into misconduct and incompetence of all agency employees, looking into issues ranging from performance to falsifying records to criminal behavior, as well as assist in navigating relations between management and labor unions regarding employee concerns.

Your Role

The role of the Deputy Director of OILR will be conducting investigations, supervising subordinate staff investigating allegations of employee misconduct, assigning work to investigators, and training new employees.

As a Deputy Director, the candidate will fill in for the Director managing investigations and dealing with labor issues when they are absent from the office. They will provide recommendations on punitive and restorative actions and advise on resolutions to organizational challenges. Additionally, the candidate will be running the Critical Driver program for the entire Agency, coordinating with General Services and driver liaisons across every Division. They will assume responsibility for OILR's internal special projects, such as digitizing old disciplinary cases and creating a training manual for future investigators.

The primary duties and responsibilities of the Deputy Director of OILR will be to

Conduct and supervise investigations into employee misconduct.

Serve as a key problem-solver and subject matter expert on disciplinary issues and dispute resolution and provide recommendations to senior staff on organizational or policy changes.

Director of Development

Position Summary

The Director of Development is a senior leadership position responsible for leading the day-to-day operations, systems, communications infrastructure, and execution framework of the Boys & Girls Clubs of Paterson and Passaic resource development function. The Director serves as the systems architect and operating leader of the Development Department, ensuring fundraising priorities are translated into workplans, calendars, assignments, accountability systems, donor engagement strategies, communications campaigns, grant processes, events, and measurable outcomes.  

The role combines development leadership with strategic communications focused primarily on fundraising, donor engagement, community visibility, corporate relationships, philanthropic positioning, and external storytelling. The Director works closely with the CEO to translate organizational priorities into a disciplined, coordinated, and sustainable development operation.  

Core Responsibilities

Development Department Leadership & Systems

• Lead the day-to-day operating framework of the Development Department and maintain the annual development workplan, fundraising calendar, grants matrix, stewardship calendar, campaign workplans, and department dashboards.  
• Establish weekly and monthly priorities, assignments, deadlines, and accountability measures; lead regular department meetings and document next steps and ownership.  
• Build and maintain standard operating procedures for prospect management, donor cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, renewals, campaigns, events, grants, and development communications.  
• Own the effectiveness and integrity of development technology and donor databases, including standards for records, segmentation, coding, gift acknowledgment, stewardship, and reporting.  
• Partner with Finance to strengthen reconciliation of gifts, pledges, restricted funds, grants, sponsorships, and other contributed revenue.  

Fundraising, Donor & Corporate Engagement

• Partner with the CEO and development leadership to execute annual contributed-revenue goals across individual giving, major gifts, corporate partnerships, foundations, grants, campaigns, events, monthly giving, and other philanthropic revenue.  
• Maintain the active prospect and solicitation pipeline, track donor movement from identification through stewardship, and ensure timely next steps after meetings, introductions, proposals, and events.  
• Manage an assigned portfolio of individual, corporate, foundation, and community relationships and participate directly in cultivation, presentations, donor meetings, and solicitations.  
• Coordinate CEO and board donor engagement by preparing background information, meeting objectives, briefing materials, solicitation strategy, and follow-up.  
• Develop corporate sponsorship and partnership opportunities and represent the organization professionally in community, civic, corporate, and philanthropic settings.  

Development-Centered Communications

• Lead an annual communications strategy aligned with the development plan and focused on donor engagement, fundraising, organizational storytelling, corporate partnerships, external affairs, and mission advancement.  
• Develop campaign messaging, annual appeals, cases for support, sponsorship materials, donor correspondence, impact reports, e-newsletters, social media storytelling, web content, and other development collateral.  
• Create a reliable internal process through which Programs and Operations provide stories, photos, outcomes, attendance information, testimonials, and other information suitable for donor-facing communications.  
• Maintain consistency in organizational messaging, brand, voice, and visual identity across external and development communications.  
• Support executive leadership with external messages related to fundraising, major organizational initiatives, community partnerships, and public-facing priorities.  

Qualifications

• Significant professional experience in nonprofit development, communications, fundraising, external affairs, marketing, donor engagement, or a related field.  
• Demonstrated ability to manage complex projects, build systems, establish workflows, and hold multiple priorities and contributors accountable.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to translate organizational impact into compelling donor-facing communications.

• Experience with donors, corporations, foundations, community partners, fundraising campaigns, events, grants, and/or direct solicitation strongly preferred.

• Experience with donor databases, CRM systems, email marketing platforms, social media, and related development technology; Blackbaud/eTapestry experience preferred.

• Ability to work effectively with executive leadership, staff, board members, donors, volunteers, consultants, and external partners while exercising sound judgment and discretion.

The Cooper Foundation is currently seeking an Executive Director (ED) to provide visionary leadership, strategic direction and operational oversight. The ED will work closely with the Board of Directors to fulfill the organization's mission and maximize community impact in the Raleigh / NC service area and oversee the Foundation’s expansion to Atlanta. The ED is responsible for working with the organization’s partners to fulfill housing stability grant requests, identifying strategic partners, fundraising, coordinating with Cooper Tacia’s finance and marketing teams, and engaging with the community.

Background

Founded in 2023, the Cooper Charitable Foundation was created with the mission to improve people’s lives by helping them secure stable housing. John Cooper, our founder, and his family come from quite humble beginnings. Each of them understands the power of stability and safety in changing the trajectory of one's life. The Cooper Foundation was created to honor his own family and to express gratitude for his journey. 

John learned about transitional housing grants while involved with Haven in Lee County, a non-profit providing assistance to victims of domestic violence and sexual assault. The Cooper Charitable Foundation adapted this concept and created Housing Stability Grants to address the critical issue of housing accessibility in our communities.

Our grants provide financial assistance in two ways – helping working people access housing or preventing people from being evicted due to life circumstances.

The majority of our grants help people pay move-in fees such as security deposits, utility deposits and first and last month’s rent. What we discovered is that many unsheltered people are working; they can pay their rent, but they can’t save enough money for the upfront fees required by most landlords. This is the biggest barrier to safe and accessible housing.

We also assist those who are working but cannot keep up with their monthly expenses due to life circumstances. Issues such as illness, mental health, a car accident, job loss, divorce or domestic violence can all impact people’s lives in different ways. We help people pay their rent and utilities or pay for car repairs or other expenses.

A Unique Shared Development Opportunity

RefugeeConnect and the Immigrant and Refugee Law Center (IRLC) are seeking an experienced development professional to serve as our Shared Development Director
, an independent contractor providing strategic fundraising and development support across both organizations.

This is not a traditional Development Director role. It is a unique opportunity to work alongside two established Greater Cincinnati nonproﬁts serving refugee and immigrant communities while helping us explore what becomes possible when mission-aligned organizations intentionally share expertise, resources, relationships, and fundraising strategy.

The Shared Development Director will support the distinct development priorities of RefugeeConnect and IRLC while also identifying opportunities for collaboration, including shared funding opportunities, donor and corporate engagement, joint fundraising initiatives, and long-range planning connected to a future regional welcoming center.

The ideal contractor will be comfortable navigating multiple organizational priorities, building relationships, developing systems, and moving between strategy and implementation. We are looking for someone who sees collaboration not as an added responsibility, but as an opportunity to build stronger and more sustainable organizations.

About the Partnership

RefugeeConnect and IRLC are two independent organizations with complementary roles in supporting refugees and immigrants throughout Greater Cincinnati.

RefugeeConnect
walks alongside refugees and their families, connecting them to resources, relationships, guidance, and opportunities to enhance their lives and thrive in our shared community.

The Immigrant and Refugee Law Center (IRLC)
provides accessible legal services to immigrant and refugee families in the Greater Cincinnati community.

Through an ongoing organizational partnership, RefugeeConnect and IRLC are investing in shared capacity that strengthens each organization individually while creating opportunities to collaborate around funding, community partnerships, and a longer-term vision for stronger regional welcoming infrastructure.

About the Contract

The Shared Development Director will provide development expertise across three interconnected areas:
Supporting the individual fundraising and development priorities of RefugeeConnect; Supporting the
individual fundraising and development priorities of IRLC; and
Identifying and advancing collaborative opportunities that beneﬁt both organizations and their shared long-term goals.

The contractor will work collaboratively with organizational leadership while maintaining the ability to independently organize and carry out the services and deliverables outlined in the contract.

Funding Strategy & Opportunity Development

Research and identify foundation, private, corporate, sponsorship, and other funding opportunities aligned with the missions and strategic priorities of both organizations.

Long-Range Funding Strategy

Research institutional funding, corporate partnerships, major donor opportunities, sponsorships, earned revenue strategies, and potential future capital support.

The contractor will contribute to collaborative visioning, relationship development, strategic planning, and early capital campaign and feasibility research associated with this longer-term initiative.

BeFit Rehabilitation provides Medicare Part B outpatient physical, occupational, and speech therapy within assisted living facilities across the Tampa/Clearwater area. As we scale, we're building the operational infrastructure to match our clinical growth — this role is central to that effort.

Position Summary
The Regional Director of Operations owns the operational and financial performance of BeFit's therapy teams across all locations. This is not a clinical-oversight-only role — it is a hands-on operational leadership position responsible for staffing efficiency, revenue cycle performance, and regulatory compliance, with direct accountability for the P&L of each care team. The ideal candidate has run multi-site outpatient therapy operations before, understands Medicare Part B billing and PTA/COTA supervision rules deeply, and has a track record of turning around underperforming locations or teams.

This role reports directly to the President and will work closely with billing, HR, and clinical leadership.

Key Responsibilities
Staffing & Productivity Management

Own visit-per-hour and revenue-per-hour benchmarks for every clinical team; identify and correct gaps between hours paid and billable production
Right-size supervising-therapist-to-assistant ratios based on actual patient census and caseload, not headcount assumptions
Partner with clinical leadership to set and enforce productivity standards across PT, OT, and ST disciplines
Build and maintain a recurring reporting cadence (weekly/monthly) that surfaces cost-per-hour vs. collections-per-hour by team and by office

Revenue Cycle & AR Oversight

Own aging AR across all payers; drive resolution of denied and zero-paid claims, with particular focus on Medicare Part B and any payer showing systemic non-payment
Work directly with billing/clearinghouse partners on root-cause analysis of denial patterns (not just resubmission)
Establish escalation protocols for payers showing abnormal payment failure rates
Monitor and report true collection rates against payer-adjudicated allowables (not charge amounts)

Compliance & Documentation

Ensure correct and consistent use of billing modifiers across all supervising clinicians
Audit documentation-to-billing alignment periodically to catch under- or over-utilization of assistant modifiers before it becomes an audit risk
Maintain compliance with CMS supervision, evaluation-complexity coding, and Part B billing requirements across all offices

Financial Accountability

Build and maintain a per-team/per-office P&L model (labor cost vs. collections) and present it to leadership on a regular cycle
Flag underperforming teams early, with a specific, data-backed diagnosis (productivity vs. collections vs. staffing mix) rather than a general "revenue is down" alert
Partner with leadership on compensation structure design (salary vs. per-visit vs. per-unit) to ensure pay models align incentives with actual reimbursement economics

Team Leadership & Multi-Site Operations

Serve as the operational point of contact across all facility partnerships
Support hiring, onboarding, and performance management for clinical and support staff in partnership with HR
Identify and roll out best practices from top-performing teams to underperforming ones

Qualifications
Required

5+ years in outpatient therapy operations management, ideally spanning multiple sites or facilities
Deep working knowledge of Medicare Part B billing, PTA/COTA supervision and reimbursement rules (including CQ/CO modifier requirements), and CPT coding for PT/OT/ST
Demonstrated experience building or managing productivity and financial performance metrics for clinical teams (not just clinical quality metrics)
Track record of identifying and resolving AR/denial issues at scale
Comfortable working directly from raw billing, payroll, and revenue data not just dashboards

Preferred

Experience specifically in ALF, SNF, or senior-living-adjacent outpatient therapy settings
Prior experience turning around an underperforming location, region, or book of business
Familiarity with per-visit and per-unit compensation models for PT/OT/ST staff and their financial implications
Clinical licensure (PT, OT, or SLP) is a plus but not required if operational/financial background is strong

Full visibility into every team's cost-per-hour vs. collections-per-hour; a clear, documented diagnosis of the 2-3 highest-impact underperforming teams or offices.
6 months:
Measurable improvement in the lowest-performing teams' hours-to-collections ratio; AR aging materially reduced on the largest payer categories; a standing compliance review process for assistant modifier usage in place.
Ongoing:
A durable, repeatable operating rhythm — not a one-time fix — where staffing decisions, compensation structure, and payer issues are caught and addressed before they become a multi-month drag on the P&L.

Lead SOC 1 and SOC 2 readiness activities, including control mapping to trust services criteria and coordination with CAT and control owners on evidence collection ahead of attestation testing.

Drive continuous improvement of SOX and SOC compliance processes, including evidence-reuse and reduction of duplicative requests to control owners, in partnership with CAT and GRC tooling teams.

Partner with policy and standards owners to ensure SOX and SOC control requirements reflect current regulatory and framework expectations as they evolve.

Lead, coach, and develop the SOX & SOC Compliance team, building bench strength and a culture of accountability, precision, and strong cross-team partnership with CAT.

10+ years of progressive experience leading first-line-of-defense SOX ITGC, SOC 1/SOC 2, technology compliance, or control governance programs, including 3+ years in a leadership role.

About Blue Cross And Blue Shield Of Minnesota

At Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Minnesota, we are committed to paving the way for everyone to achieve their healthiest life. We are looking for dedicated and motivated individuals who share our vision of transforming healthcare. As a Blue Cross associate, you are joining a culture that is built on values of succeeding together, finding a better way, and doing the right thing. If you are ready to make a difference, join us.

The Impact You Will Have

The Program Director, Program Integrity is responsible for developing and leading the enterprise-wide internal and external strategy, governance, and outcomes of the organization’s Fraud, Waste, and Abuse (FWA) prevention and detection program. This leadership role drives execution across multiple stakeholder teams and ensures a proactive, analytics-enabled approach to program integrity across all lines of business, in line with affordability of care objectives and regulatory requirements. This role is also responsible for external engagement with government organizations and stakeholders and driving Program Integrity Subcommittee activities. The ideal candidate brings at least 7+ years of deep experience in program integrity, fraud, waste and abuse (FWA), Special Investigations Unit (SIU), payment integrity, compliance, and/or related regulatory environments, along with a strong understanding of government-sponsored healthcare programs, particularly Medicaid. This individual has a proven track record of influencing senior leaders, building cross-functional alignment, and partnering effectively with external stakeholders such as regulators, government agencies, and industry organizations. A strategic and highly credible leader who can establish program rigor, navigate complex business and regulatory challenges, and translate analytics and insights into meaningful action and organizational outcomes.

What You’ll Do

Develop and execute the enterprise Program Integrity strategy, aligning fraud, waste, and abuse (FWA) initiatives with affordability goals, regulatory requirements, and organizational priorities.
Develop and maintain relationships with appropriate regulators, law enforcement, and industry groups. These relationships will include Minnesota elected and appointed leaders at the state, county, and local level; members of the U.S. Congress, and healthcare and business organizations, CMS, and DHS in an ever-increasing regulatory environment as health reform moves forward. Other external relationships may include the national Blue Cross and Blue Shield Association and other Blue Cross Blue Shield plans
Oversee enterprise FWA risk management, including prevention, detection, monitoring, governance, and continuous improvement of risk mitigation strategies.
Provide strategic leadership for Program Integrity governance, including executive and board-level reporting, committee oversight, and organizational thought leadership.
Ensure compliance with federal and state regulations, support audits and investigations, and maintain relationships with regulators, industry organizations, law enforcement, and government stakeholders.
Lead development of analytics, dashboards, KPIs, and reporting to measure program effectiveness, financial impact, savings, and risk exposure while translating insights for executive leadership.

How You’ll Do It

Lead cross-functional collaboration across clinical, network, pharmacy, operations, finance, legal, compliance, SIU, and analytics teams to strengthen program integrity controls and mitigate risk.
Influence enterprise initiatives, payment models, products, and vendor strategies to embed program integrity and compliance requirements.
Partner with Finance and business leaders to validate savings methodologies, quantify cost avoidance, and advance enterprise affordability and total cost of care objectives.
Performs additional responsibilities consistent with the scope and level of the role, as assigned.

Required Skills & Experience

7+ years of related compliance/fraud, waste, and abuse (FWA) professional experience.
Bachelor’s degree; in lieu of a degree, an additional two years of relevant experience beyond the qualifications listed above may be accepted.

Preferred Skills & Experience

Master's degree in related field.
Ability to translate complex information into actionable messaging, actively listen to diverse perspectives, and drive alignment across cross-functional priorities.
Ability to analyze complex challenges, evaluate tradeoffs, and collaborate with stakeholders to reach effective, lasting solutions.
Ability to effectively organize work, balance shifting priorities, and manage time across multiple workstreams to meet commitments.
Business analysis expertise, regulatory research, and ability to translate regulatory requirement into operation.
Ability to interpret and apply applicable federal and state regulations.
Healthcare or insurance industry experience.
Experience with Medicare/Medicaid regulatory programs.
Experience with CMS, DOH, and state regulatory filings.
Experience drafting responses or presenting to boards, compliance committees, or regulatory bodies.

Licensure/Certifications

Preferred Certifications - Certified Compliance & Ethics Professional (CCEP) - Society of Corporate Compliance and Ethics (SCCE), Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE) - Association of Certified Fraud Examiners (ACFE), Certified in Healthcare Compliance (CHC) - Health Care Compliance Association (HCCA), Certified in Healthcare Privacy Compliance (CHPC) - Health Care Compliance Association (HCCA)

We come together in the office two days each week – most teams designate at least one anchor day to ensure team interaction. These in-person moments foster relationships, creativity, and alignment.
